Turn the brink into a second chance.
Your card healing and control grow stronger as your health falls. Recover after a heavy hit, then disrupt your opponent before their next burst.
At the Brink strengthens card healing, stuns, and draw disruption as health is lost. At 25% health, its base healing multiplier is 1.60 and its control multiplier is 1.30.
Chain recovery into control. Low health empowers your innate ability, but leaves little room for delay: play that crucial heal in time.
Further strengthens healing and control after At the Brink, making your decisive plays count.

Let each chain ignite the next.

Emberchain advances draw charge based on the number of core-element cards played together and consecutive plays with that same core. Stronger chains also draw cards immediately.
Focused elemental plays build momentum. With a five-card hand limit, play promptly and keep the chain going to turn extra draws into pressure.

Hold your health. Hold your ground.
High health makes every shield stronger. Absorb pressure behind a steady defense, then choose when to trade health for a burst of your own.
Mountainward increases shield gain in proportion to your current health, with a base multiplier of 1.45 at full health. Stay healthy to keep your defenses strong.
Protect your health before building shields. Health-cost cards lower your health before their effects resolve. Guardians alone also benefit from the Bulwark set’s extra damage reduction.
Adds extra shield after shield-gain effects resolve. Upgrading it increases that bonus and reinforces your defenses.
Reliable shields that reward staying healthy.

A class identity. A deck of your own.
Shared cards work with every class; class cards belong to their own class. Bring up to one shared legendary and one class legendary together.
Classes have no combat element of their own. Choose cards and gear that suit your innate ability; a class’s visual identity does not lock its deck to one element.
Your signature weapon equips automatically and is never lost on death. Upgrade it with equipment fragments to develop your innate ability.

Glowing relic cards above moonlit ruins

Three classes. Twenty cards of your own. Chain cards in real time, overcome monsters, and face travelers in the same cell. Push deeper or extract with your haul: every play is a choice about getting home.
Step into the unknown. Choose when to return.

Relicbound (Veilhaul) is an online card extraction game. Prepare at camp, then enter a realm shaped by five elements. Your deck sets the pace and your route sets the risk. Weigh the promise of going deeper against the haul you could bring home.
Combine shared cards with your class cards. Play in real time with up to five cards in hand; played cards enter the discard pile and are reshuffled when your deck runs out.
Play damage cards of one element together for stronger resonance. Opposing elements trade some damage for stronger recovery. Monster resistances and enemy gear change which plays are worth making.
Go inward. Know when to leave.
Advance from the outer ring toward the core, with no retreat to outer layers. Travelers sharing a cell may clash in a duel. Find an extraction point and clear your monsters to bring your haul home.
After clearing your monsters in a cell, choose gear, equipment shards, or immediate healing. Build your reserves or recover before pushing deeper.

Your expedition pack limits what you carry; secure slots protect their contents. Death leaves your five armor pieces and unsecured supplies as loot for other travelers. Your cards and signature weapon remain yours.
Use extracted warrior and class souls to develop your cards, and equipment shards to upgrade gear. Restock with gold or trade eligible equipment at the player market before your next expedition.
Elements shape damage and resistance; effect affixes shape your build. Balance quality, upgrades, and set bonuses when choosing what to wear.
Five armor slots. One battle plan.
All five slots can carry any element. Each piece provides damage and resistance for its element. Sets require matching effect affixes, not matching elements.
Armor quality runs from white, green, blue, and purple to orange and red. Equip at most one orange or red armor piece in total. Purple gear may carry an effect affix; orange and red gear always do.
Upgrade armor to +5. Levels +1 through +3 cost equipment shards; +4 and +5 each also require one equipment piece of the same quality. Upgraded armor can still be lost on death.
A weapon bound to your class

Brinkstaff, Emberfuel, and Mountainshield equip automatically with their classes and strengthen innate abilities. They cannot be unequipped or lost on death. All upgrades cost only shards, including +4 and +5.
Strike, Bulwark, and Vitality are three effect affixes. Different elements can form the same affix set. These effects activate only when the set requirement is met.
matching affix pieces normally activate a set

Add direct damage to your offense
Adds direct damage to your attacks, supporting offensive decks. Strike damage does not bypass a Guardian’s Bulwark damage reduction.
Improves shield gain for every class. Its additional damage reduction applies only to Guardians, before damage is taken from shields or health.
Strengthens healing and raises the effective health cap, up to 140% of base maximum health. All classes can benefit; the shield cap does not increase.
Three purple Bulwark pieces activate the set even if their elements are wood, fire, and earth. Two purple pieces do not; one orange Bulwark piece plus one purple Bulwark piece does.
Red gear · A shared server limit

Red gear is a rare reward for high-difficulty expeditions. Under the planned system, each server can generate at most one red item per week, shared across all players and maps. The quota resets on Monday at 04:00 in the server’s time zone; unused quota does not carry over, and a drop is not guaranteed each week.

Once Doom I and higher difficulties open, defeating the Chaos Realm’s core Boss has a 0.4% chance to award an extra red item while the server quota remains available, separate from the three-choice reward. Eligible red gear brought home can also be traded for gold on the player market. Doom difficulties and red-gear drops are not yet available in the current prototype.
Red gear also rolls one exclusive affix, which cannot be rerolled. These are future features; regular red-gear acquisition is not available in the current prototype.

Your discoveries. Someone else’s next build.
Set your own prices for spare gear at the auction house, or find equipment that fits your deck. Trading currently uses gold; a diamond auction house is planned for high-quality equipment.

Sellers set their listing prices and buyers purchase at the listed price, settled in gold. Eligible equipment must be brought home, unequipped, and unbound. Turn spare loot into supplies for your next expedition.

Listing is free, with up to eight active listings lasting 48 hours each. Unsold items return to your inventory. Completed sales deduct a 10% fee from the seller’s proceeds, with a minimum of one gold; buyers pay no extra fee.

Future plans add diamond listings and settlement for orange and red equipment while retaining gold trading. Gold and diamond listings use their respective currencies. The diamond auction house is not yet available.

The auction house trades eligible equipment. Cards, warrior souls, class souls, equipment shards, expedition packs, health potions, and signature weapons cannot be listed. Supplies still inside an expedition cannot be sold either.
